solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rebecca's written in it for Adam

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca is narrated by its unnamed heroine as 'I'
second meaning: in Genesis Adam is the first human being ever made

explanation.surface: A note that Rebecca has written something inside a book intended for a man called Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebecca looks like a girl writing a card, but it is du Maurier's novel; Adam looks like the recipient, but he is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical narrating voice of 'I' shares its name with the very first human, the biblical Adam.

clue.text: Brave flees as bear eventually becomes distressed

indicators.note: something distressed is upset and disordered, so the gathered letters are jumbled
eventually means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word before it is used

explanation.surface: A courageous person runs off while a bear grows upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brave shows no fear, which is exactly what the word describes.

clue.text: Novelist right to support Republican rally

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting something means sitting underneath it, so these pieces follow the party letter

parts.note: Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose
right as an intensifier, as in 'right good' or 'very good'

explanation.surface: A writer is properly backing a Republican political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' means very, in the old intensifying sense of 'the Right Honourable' or 'a right mess'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally, as in markets or health, is a recovery from a low point.

clue.text: Rout engineered by Tottenham's head coach

indicators.note: engineered means constructed or contrived, so the letters are rebuilt into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A football thrashing masterminded by the Tottenham Hotspur manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club, and 'head coach' looks like one job title; it splits into the selection indicator and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a private teacher who prepares a pupil, the same as a tutor.

clue.text: Milk's put to good use

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to milk someone is to take unfair advantage of them
second meaning: to make the most of a resource

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as milk being a useful drink; both halves are verbs for drawing benefit from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of drawing maximum advantage, one unfairly and one productively.

clue.text: Separate pieces of advice about containing Liberal in revolt

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word for advice is read backwards
containing means holding inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: people who are up in arms are rising in revolt

explanation.surface: Political advice concerning a rebellious Liberal, treated as several separate items.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to part company, which is what a couple does when they split up.

clue.text: Spooner's to get relative to sit in a certain way for a bit of protection

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of a pair of words

parts.words: relative to sit in a certain way
parts.note: a niece is a relative, and to pose is to sit in a particular way for a portrait

explanation.surface: Spooner wants a family member to adopt a particular posture as a safety measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of POSE and NIECE. A nosepiece is the guard on a helmet that shields the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece is the part of a helmet or visor that guards the nose, so a small piece of armour.

clue.text: Poet mostly found in pub

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A poet who can usually be found drinking at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is the room or premises where drinks are served, the same as a pub.

clue.text: Phone left in boudoir

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that follows it

parts.note: a bower is a lady's private chamber, an old word for a boudoir

explanation.surface: A telephone that has been left lying in a lady's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The blower is British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is informal British slang for a telephone, from old speaking tubes you blew into.

clue.text: King in pursuit of support

parts.note: R for Rex, Latin for king
chasing something means going after it

explanation.surface: A monarch chasing backing for his cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is one of the sloping beams that hold up a roof, a structural support.

clue.text: Tie company located in street near the centre of Doncaster

indicators.note: near means right beside, so the two pieces are placed next to each other
the centre of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter alone
something located in another thing is placed inside it

explanation.surface: A firm's address on a road in central Doncaster, which sells ties.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster and Ascot are both English racecourse towns, which makes the place feel like the answer's neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad cravat-style neckcloth, a kind of tie worn with formal dress.

clue.text: No longer available with gloss finish

indicators.note: with puts the two pieces side by side, the second leading here

parts.note: gloss and polish are both a shiny surface
a dish that is off the menu cannot be ordered

explanation.surface: A product discontinued in its glossy paint finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss finish' looks like a single paint term; 'finish' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off food or a task is to finish it completely and quickly.

clue.text: Start of long argument with vicar over filling it with a plant

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
a filling goes inside something, so these letters go within the short word
turned over means flipped, so the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A long-running quarrel with the vicar about planting something in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverworts are small non-flowering green plants related to mosses.

clue.text: A musical composition from Queen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single work of music
second meaning: the queen is one of the playing figures in chess, the question mark showing it is an example

explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band whose song this might be; it is the chess queen, an example flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is both a single work of music and any of the carved figures moved on a chessboard.

clue.text: Arrange for clear up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put things in order
second meaning: to resolve a problem or tidy a mess

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as booking someone to tidy up; both halves are phrasal senses of the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting out a room arranges its contents; sorting out a dispute clears it up.

clue.text: Makes too high an estimate of more than one bowling team's efficiency

definitions.text: Makes too high an estimate of
definitions.meaning: first meaning: values something more than it deserves

definitions.text: more than one bowling team's efficiency
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split differently: plural of a cricket term for how fast a fielding side gets through its overs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, and a side's over rate is how many overs it bowls per hour; 'more than one' makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to estimate too highly; read as two words it is the cricket statistic in plural.

clue.text: Take a brief look at reserve's back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to keep something is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Glance quickly at the reverse side of the substitutes' bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve's back' suggests a back-up player; the 's is 'is', and back turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick, often furtive glance.

clue.text: Disinclined to speak about capsizing it in wind

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down entry the short word is turned over
in places the combined letters inside the final word

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
to wind is to turn, as with a handle

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to talk about their boat overturning in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the weather that capsized the boat, but it is the verb that rhymes with 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is habitually silent and reserved, unwilling to talk.

clue.text: Centre ground ally oddly neglected of late

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the word's letters are rearranged
neglecting the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of ally

explanation.surface: A centrist political partner has been ignored lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre ground' looks like the political middle; ground is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late and recently both mean in the period just past.

clue.text: State of confusion caused by footballer missing international

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for the next word is removed

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when a footballer fails to turn up for an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a muddled, disordered situation.

clue.text: Almost fall for extremely sweet unassuming Cockney

indicators.note: a London Cockney accent famously drops the aitch at the start of words
at its extremes means just the two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of sweet

explanation.surface: A modest, very sweet East Ender nearly trips over.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip and nearly fall.

clue.text: Agreed to differ over nuclear bomb

indicators.note: letters that differ are changed from how they were, so they are rearranged
in an across entry, over means placed before, so the next piece follows

explanation.surface: Two sides agree to disagree about the atom bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreed to differ' is a stock phrase, but agreed is the fodder and N joins it before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small explosive bomb thrown by hand.

clue.text: Forward to follow up earlier stroke of luck

indicators.note: earlier means coming first, so this piece goes at the front
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
to forward a letter is to send it on

explanation.surface: Advice to follow up an earlier lucky shot by sending the ball on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow up' looks like a phrasal verb; it splits into the synonym and the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected and welcome piece of good fortune.

clue.text: Frequently repeated slogan evident in German translation

indicators.note: evident in means visible inside, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A catchphrase that shows up when something is rendered into German.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a statement or phrase repeated often, originally a chant in meditation.

clue.text: Dog tucked into writer's soup

indicators.note: tucked into means slipped inside, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
to dog someone is to tag along after them

explanation.surface: A dog helps itself to an author's soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating the soup; it is the instruction to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, from the French word for it.

clue.text: Love affair with old American actress not likely at first

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Dorothy Lamour, star of the Road to... films with Bob Hope and Bing Crosby

indicators.note: at first points to only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A romance with an old Hollywood star that seemed improbable from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not likely' reads as an idiom of refusal; split up, it removes the first letter of likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is French for love, used in English for a romantic or secret affair.

clue.text: Durer fine about being exposed to criticism

indicators.note: about can mean all around or in disorder, so the letters are turned around

explanation.surface: The German artist Albrecht Dürer is fine with being attacked by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under fire, literally being shot at, figuratively means facing strong criticism.

clue.text: Go over letters from Deirdre Capone

indicators.note: letters from means a run of letters is lifted from the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: Reading through correspondence from a woman named Deirdre Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence from a gangster's relative; it signals a string of letters lifted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Easily managed to find motorists to take part in races around island

indicators.note: taking part in something means joining inside it, so these letters go within the races

parts.note: the TT races, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: turned around means facing the opposite way, so the island is read backwards

parts.note: Elba, the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Drivers who enter races round an island are easily handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable means docile and easy to control or deal with.

clue.text: Consider in advance protecting Unionist in court

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it
in places the combined letters inside the final word

parts.note: on means ahead, as a clock running fast is on

explanation.surface: Weigh up beforehand the case for defending a Unionist in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To count someone lucky is to consider or regard them as such.

clue.text: There's no head on weak beer

indicators.note: having no head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: pale means weak or feeble, as in a pale imitation

explanation.surface: A complaint that a thin, watery beer has no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is the froth on beer, which makes the deletion feel like part of the pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: Dean's wrong to maintain pressure on girl to go

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed beside, so the girl's name follows
maintaining something means holding it, so a letter is kept inside
wrong means not right, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A college dean wrongly presses a young woman to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go' is the British euphemism for needing the toilet; spending a penny comes from the coin once needed to unlock public lavatories.
explanation.definitionFit: Spend a penny is a polite British idiom for urinating, a euphemism for needing to go.
